forks.decision: External tasks run fully native with a local checkout without upstream history, a local uv venv or Go/Rust toolchain, and our replay of the instance's FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests; no Docker
One evolutionary loop mutates code and text; a candidate is a commit
The loop engine is GEPA optimize_anything with repeat runs on frontier candidates
The loop may mutate only src and prompts; winners land as human-reviewed draft PRs
The judge labels per-task applicability and critiques each rollout for reflection only; grader correctness is the only objective
The Phase 4 power gate is retired; every paid run requires an explicit spend ceiling

contradictions: The judge critique carries grader inputs into reflection, which breaks cross-curd invariant 2 (spec line 96: 'No optimizer-side model reads grader inputs ... never correctness_reason, ground-truth strings, gold patches, or held-out test source or output') and the F-5 rationale (line 108). The interface sketch is judge.critique(row, trajectory) -> str (line 148). The stored row carries correctness_reason (benchmark/run.py:851), which holds 'Missing: {required}' ground-truth strings (benchmark/tasks/base.py:178-180) and the last 1200 characters of held-out test output (benchmark/tasks/gin_render_context_tasks.py:152-153). Approach step 3 (line 89) also has the judge read ground truth, trusted references, and gold patches. AC-4 (line 117) then passes critiques into reflection when the judge is calibrated. AC-2 (line 115) strips grader text only from fields 'kept from grading', and a critique is not one of those. No parent statement says the critique input is stripped or that a critique is screened for grader text. The AC-2 test (line 128) seeds SECRET_GT only into correctness_reason, and the AC-4 test uses a stub judge that will not echo it. So an implementation that hands the raw row to judge.critique and forwards the critique into reflection passes every parent test while ground truth and held-out test output reach the reflection model and the proposer.

Contaminated rollouts are not kept out of the score or out of the reflective records, which contradicts invariant 2 (line 96) and the F-5 rationale that 'the loop cannot steer the score through ... leaked tests' (line 108). Approach step 2 (line 88) only marks a row contaminated when its trajectory fetches upstream source or reads the harness data directory. Risks (line 161) concedes that agent cells have no isolation; the gin held-out tests sit in benchmark/tasks/gin_render_context_fixtures (gin_render_context_tasks.py:17, 63-66). AC-2 (line 115) requires each reflective record to include every tool call's full output untruncated, so a contaminated trajectory puts held-out test source or the upstream fix straight into the record. AC-4 (line 117) scores mean grader correctness with no exclusion for contaminated rows. The loop mutates the agent-facing prompts/** and src/** (F-4), so it can evolve instructions that make agents read held-out tests or fetch upstream fixes, and those correct-but-contaminated rows raise the score. No parent AC or invariant says what the contaminated flag does to the score, frontier acceptance, or reflective records, and no parent test seeds a contaminated row.
acceptance_gaps: No parent test checks the positive branch of G-1, G-2, or G-3 (Test Contracts AC-1 row, spec line 127). test_paid_panel_requires_every_task_family covers only refusals: it is parametrized over panels that each lack one member. It has no positive control in which the complete fixture panel, with an admitted FeatureBench task, gin_edit_render_context, the three local hard tasks, and the Go and Rust instances, starts a paid run and reaches the runner. A panels.load_panel or admission check that refuses every panel, or admits no external task, therefore passes every parent test. Then no FeatureBench task ever runs in the harness, and the Gin and cherry-picked tasks are never in a runnable panel. Risks line 159 accepts a refusal only when no FeatureBench task survives native admission, not as the default behavior. The positive outcome of 'FeatureBench tasks run in our harness' and 'is in the panel' is never observed.
